purpose: A descriptor for the memory-bomb enforcement check. The child allocates memory in 64 MiB slabs until it is killed. On Linux (CI) RLIMIT_AS (derived from policy rss_bytes) kills the child with MemoryError/SIGSEGV; on macOS RLIMIT_AS cannot be lowered below the current hard limit, so the wall watchdog is the backstop. Either way the run does not complete and no receipt is written.

platform_split.linux: RLIMIT_AS is enforced; the child is killed when its address space exceeds policy.default.rss_bytes (1.5 GiB in M1). The child exits non-zero (MemoryError); the runner reports resource_limit or failed.
platform_split.macos: RLIMIT_AS cannot be lowered (the kernel rejects it); the wall watchdog kills the child at wall_seconds. The runner reports timeout. The other limits (CPU, FSIZE, NOFILE, NPROC) are still applied.

expected_behavior.rss_bytes_assertion: usage.rss_bytes > 0 (the run consumed real memory before being bounded)

notes: bomb.v1 is a test-only adapter (loaded only under SRL_RUNNER_TEST_ADAPTERS=1). The gate accepts {resource_limit, timeout, failed} as a bounded outcome and asserts receipt_written is False.
